# What this file does

Starting from the end of the phenotypic burn-in (file 01), four breeding programmes are run
for `r params$n_gs_gen` generations **from the same starting population**:

| Scenario | Selection criterion | Mating |
|---|---|---|
| PHENO | herd-corrected phenotypes (cows), dam index (bulls), NTM weights | random |
| GS_NTM | genomic EBV, NTM index (May 2026 weights, file 00) - current Nordic practice | random |
| GS_NTM_NUE35 | as GS_NTM plus NUE weight 0.35 (= Saved Feed weight) | random |
| GS_NTM_NUE75 | as GS_NTM plus NUE weight 0.75 | random |
| GS_NTM_NUE35_MUN | as GS_NTM_NUE35 plus MUN weight -0.35 (lower MUN = less N lost in urine) | random |
| GS_NTM_NUE<nn>_CH4 | NUE weight plus the CH4 weight at the knee of the CH4 weight sweep (file 00 picks both; 17-trait set: NUE 0.75, CH4 -0.50) | random |
| GS_NTM_NUE35_MATE | as GS_NTM_NUE35 | mate allocation with expected progeny F < `r params$f_max` |
| GS_NTM_NUE35_OCS | as GS_NTM_NUE35, optimum contribution selection of bulls (target dF `ocs_dF`) | mate allocation within OCS contributions |

The two NUE indices differ from GS_NTM **only in the NUE weight**, so differences in any
trait are attributable to that one weight. The earlier illustrative indices (GS_PROD, GS_NUE,
GS_NUE_noMUN; superseded) are in `archive_illustrative_index/`.

Genomic EBVs come from **SNP effects** (SNP-BLUP), so EBV = Σ dosage x marker effect.
Training is strictly forward: calves are selected before their own (or sisters') CFIT
records exist, matching the pipeline timeline (genotyping year 2, phenotypes from year 4).

Each call runs one replicate (`rep_id`); replicates use seed + `rep_id`, with the same random
stream start for every scenario within a replicate, so scenarios are compared **paired**.

# Load burn-in state

```{r load}
st <- readRDS(file.path(params$sim_dir, "burnin_state.rds")); SP <- st$SP
# Memory: only the last two burn-in generations of cows are used below (training set)
st$kept_cows <- st$kept_cows[as.integer(sub(" .*", "", names(st$kept_cows))) >= max(as.integer(sub(" .*", "", names(st$kept_cows)))) - 1]
invisible(gc())
memlog <- function(tag) progress(params$scenarios[1], " ", tag, " | R memory in use (MB): ", round(sum(gc()[, 2])))
memlog("state loaded")
phen0 <- fread(file.path(params$sim_dir, "phenotypes.csv"))
phen0 <- phen0[generation >= max(generation) - 1]          # only the last two burn-in generations are used
trend0 <- fread(file.path(params$sim_dir, "trend_burnin.csv"))
h2 <- fread(if (file.exists(file.path(params$sim_dir, "h2_used.csv"))) file.path(params$sim_dir, "h2_used.csv") else "params/h2.csv")   # h2 of this burn-in (sensitivity sets differ)
split <- fread("params/breed_country_split.csv"); herds_tab <- fread("params/herds.csv")
traits <- st$traits; nT <- length(traits); breeds <- c("HOL", "RDC", "JER")
countries <- unique(split$country); nC <- length(countries)
all_herds <- herds_tab$herd; herd_country <- herds_tab$country
gxe <- st$gxe_rg < 1
n_cow <- round(split[, sum(n), by = breed][match(breeds, breed), V1] * st$design$scale)
names(n_cow) <- breeds
sires_n <- st$design$sires_per_breed
burn_end <- max(phen0$generation)
cat("Start generation:", burn_end, "| cows per breed:", paste(n_cow, collapse = "/"),
    "| sires:", paste(sires_n, collapse = "/"), "| GxE scenario:", gxe, "\n")
```

# Breeding goal and selection indices

Index weights act on **standardised** breeding values (divided by the genetic SD of each
trait at the end of burn-in). They are the **NTM sub-index weights (May 2026)**, mapped onto
the simulated traits in file 00 (`params/index_weights.csv`), and are **breed-specific**.
NUE, MUN, CH4 and LNVAR have no NTM weight; NUE is added at 0.35 or 0.75, MUN at -0.35 and CH4 at -0.50 (file 00). Saved Feed (SF) carries the NTM Saved Feed weight.

```{r index}
iw <- fread("params/index_weights.csv")
ntm_of <- function(s) sub("_(MATE|OCS)$", "", s)          # MATE/OCS use their base index
idx_def <- fread("params/index_definitions.csv")            # indices defined in file 00
all_scen <- c("PHENO", idx_def$index, "GS_NTM_NUE35_MATE", "GS_NTM_NUE35_OCS")
W_idx <- setNames(lapply(all_scen, function(s) {
  base <- if (s == "PHENO") "GS_NTM" else ntm_of(s)
  stopifnot(base %in% iw$index)
  setNames(lapply(breeds, function(b) { x <- iw[index == base & breed == b]; setNames(x$weight, x$trait)[traits] }), breeds)
}), all_scen)
# "CH4_KNEE" = the methane index chosen in file 00 (its name depends on which NUE weight wins the sweep)
scen_req <- ifelse(params$scenarios == "CH4_KNEE", idx_def[ch4 != 0, index][1], params$scenarios)
stopifnot(!anyNA(unlist(W_idx)), all(scen_req %in% all_scen))
kable(idx_def, caption = "Extra weights (per genetic SD) added to the NTM weights, from file 00")
kable(dcast(iw[weight != 0 | trait %in% c("NUE", "MUN", "CH4")], trait ~ index + breed, value.var = "weight"), digits = 3,
      caption = "Index weights per genetic SD (all other traits 0)")
is_ocs  <- function(s) grepl("_OCS$", s)
is_mate <- function(s) grepl("_(MATE|OCS)$", s)

# genetic SD per trait at the end of burn-in (standardisation constant, fixed thereafter)
sdA0 <- sapply(traits, function(tr) sd(phen0[generation == burn_end][[paste0("TBV_", tr)]]))
round(sdA0, 3)
```

# Simulation functions

`make_pheno()` and `assign_blocks()` are identical to file 01 (single-breed herds;
herd-generation effects; breed-specific residual variance fixed at burn-in values).

```{r fns}
varE <- st$varE; herd_sd <- st$herd_sd
herd_breed <- herds_tab$breed
# single-breed herds (CFIT farms, file 00): cows of breed b go to b's herds, countries in proportion
# to the CFIT split (largest remainder), herds filled evenly - identical to file 01
assign_blocks <- function(n, gen, b) {
  sp <- split[breed == b][match(countries, country)]
  x <- n * sp$n / sum(sp$n); k <- floor(x); left <- n - sum(k)
  if (left > 0) { o <- order(-(x - k), seq_along(x)); k[o[seq_len(left)]] <- k[o[seq_len(left)]] + 1 }
  cty <- rep(countries, k); hrd <- character(n)
  for (c in countries) { i <- which(cty == c); h <- all_herds[herd_breed == b & herd_country == c]
    if (length(i)) hrd[i] <- rep(h, length.out = length(i))[sample.int(length(i))] }
  o <- sample.int(n); data.table(country = cty[o], herd = hrd[o], generation = gen)
}
draw_herd_z <- function() matrix(rnorm(length(all_herds) * nT), ncol = nT,
                                 dimnames = list(all_herds, traits))
own_country_G <- function(pop, cty) {
  G <- gv(pop)
  if (!gxe) { colnames(G) <- traits; return(G) }
  t(sapply(seq_len(nInd(pop)), function(k) {
    ci <- match(cty[k], countries); G[k, ((ci - 1) * nT + 1):(ci * nT)] }))
}
# breeding goal value = average over countries (identical to own-country value if no GxE)
goal_G <- function(pop) {
  G <- gv(pop); if (!gxe) { colnames(G) <- traits; return(G) }
  A <- Reduce(`+`, lapply(seq_len(nC), function(ci) G[, ((ci - 1) * nT + 1):(ci * nT)])) / nC
  colnames(A) <- traits; A
}
make_pheno <- function(pop, breed, blocks, herd_z) {
  G <- own_country_G(pop, blocks$country); colnames(G) <- traits
  H <- sweep(herd_z, 2, herd_sd[, breed], `*`)
  E <- matrix(rnorm(nInd(pop) * nT, 0, rep(sqrt(varE[, breed]), each = nInd(pop))), ncol = nT)
  P <- G + H[blocks$herd, , drop = FALSE] + E; colnames(P) <- traits
  P
}
trunc_i <- function(p) dnorm(qnorm(1 - p)) / p            # selection intensity, truncation
```

## SNP-BLUP (marker effects)

For each trait: **y\*** = **Wβ** + **e**, fixed effects (breed x generation, herd x generation)
absorbed exactly: **W\*** = (I - P~X~)W, **y\*** = (I - P~X~)y. Then
β = (W\*'W\* + λI)^-1^ W\*'y\* = W\*'(W\*W\*' + λI)^-1^ y\* (the two forms are algebraically identical;
the second needs an n x n rather than an SNP x SNP eigen-decomposition, which matters with 50k SNP),
solved for all traits with one eigen-decomposition.
λ = σ^2^~e~ / σ^2^~β~, σ^2^~β~ = σ^2^~A~ / Σ2pq, with σ^2^~A~ = h^2^ var(y\*) using the
**assumed heritability** from file 00 (breed-weighted). Fixing variance ratios at assumed
values is how routine evaluations run between variance-component re-estimations.

```{r snpblup}
h2_mix <- function(brd) sapply(traits, function(tr)
  sum(table(factor(brd, breeds)) * unlist(h2[code == tr, ..breeds])) / length(brd))

snp_blup <- function(Mtr, Ytr, Xdf) {
  X  <- model.matrix(~ factor(bg) + factor(hg), data = Xdf)
  q  <- qr(X); X <- X[, q$pivot[seq_len(q$rank)], drop = FALSE]
  XtXi <- solve(crossprod(X))
  absorb <- function(A) A - X %*% (XtXi %*% crossprod(X, A))     # P A, with P = I - X(X'X)^-1 X'
  p <- colMeans(Mtr) / 2; k2pq <- 2 * sum(p * (1 - p))
  # dual (n x n) form, exact for ridge regression: (W'W + lam I)^-1 W'y = W'(WW' + lam I)^-1 y,
  # here with fixed effects absorbed, Ws = P W. With ~50k SNP and ~6k cows this needs one n x n
  # eigen-decomposition instead of a 50k x 50k one.
  # Memory, 7 GB machine: Ws is never formed. Ws Ws' = P (W W') P, with W W' summed
  # over blocks of SNP, and Ws' z = W' (P z). Same algebra as before, so the same SNP effects
  # (up to floating-point rounding).
  K <- matrix(0, nrow(Mtr), nrow(Mtr))
  for (cols in split(seq_len(ncol(Mtr)), ceiling(seq_len(ncol(Mtr)) / 2000))) K <- K + tcrossprod(Mtr[, cols, drop = FALSE] - 1)
  K <- absorb(t(absorb(K))); K <- (K + t(K)) / 2                 # P K P, symmetrised against rounding
  e <- eigen(K, symmetric = TRUE); rm(K); invisible(gc())
  Ys <- absorb(Ytr)
  rhs <- crossprod(e$vectors, Ys)
  hh <- h2_mix(Xdf$breed)
  beta <- sapply(seq_len(nT), function(j) {
    vy <- var(Ys[, j]); lam <- (1 - hh[j]) * vy / (hh[j] * vy / k2pq)
    Pz <- absorb(e$vectors %*% (rhs[, j] / (pmax(e$values, 0) + lam)))
    as.vector(crossprod(Mtr, Pz)) - sum(Pz)                         # (M - 1)' P z
  })
  colnames(beta) <- traits; beta
}
```

## ssGBLUP alternative (model test)

The aim was to test SNP-BLUP against ssGBLUP inside the breeding programme and keep the one with the
higher response that does not need a much longer run time. The single-step version here uses the
same training cows, the same fixed effects (breed x generation, herd x generation) and the same
assumed heritabilities as SNP-BLUP, so the only differences are (1) `n_nongeno_ss` extra cows that
have CFIT records but no genotypes enter through the pedigree, and (2) the pedigree itself.

* H^-1^ = A^-1^ + [0, 0; 0, G~b~^-1^ - A~22~^-1^], with G~b~ = 0.95 (a + bG) + 0.05 A~22~ - the
  compatibility method chosen in file 02 (`ssgblup_choice_*.csv`).
* Animal-model mixed-model equations with λ = (1 - h^2^)/h^2^ per trait, solved with a sparse
  Cholesky factor; the sparsity pattern is the same for all traits, so the factor is computed once and
  only updated numerically per trait (`Matrix::update`).
* Selection candidates (calves, bulls) are not in H. Their GEBVs come from SNP effects back-solved from
  the genotyped training cows, u = Z'G~b~^-1^â~g~ / Σ2pq (Wang et al. 2012, *Genet Res* 94:73; the
  "indirect prediction" route used in routine single-step evaluations). Because the returned SNP effects
  are centred on the training allele frequencies, GEBVs differ from the SNP-BLUP scale by a constant per
  trait, which does not change any ranking.

```{r ssgblup_fn}
ss_gblup <- function(Mtr, trn_g, trn_ng, ped_all, depth = 3) {
  ids_g <- as.character(trn_g$id); ids_n <- as.character(trn_ng$id)
  # pedigree traced `depth` generations back from all training cows
  keep <- c(ids_g, ids_n); cur <- keep
  for (d in seq_len(depth)) {
    pp <- ped_all[id %in% cur]; par <- unique(na.omit(c(pp$sire, pp$dam)))
    cur <- setdiff(par, keep); keep <- c(keep, cur); if (!length(cur)) break
  }
  P <- ped_all[id %in% keep, .(id, dam, sire)]
  P[!(dam %in% id), dam := NA]; P[!(sire %in% id), sire := NA]
  Pp <- nadiv::prepPed(as.data.frame(P))
  Ainv <- nadiv::makeAinv(Pp)$Ainv; dimnames(Ainv) <- list(Pp[, 1], Pp[, 1])
  # G (VanRaden 1) on the training cows' allele frequencies; A22^-1 by partition
  p <- colMeans(Mtr) / 2; k2pq <- 2 * sum(p * (1 - p))
  Z <- sweep(Mtr, 2, 2 * p); G <- tcrossprod(Z) / k2pq
  oid <- setdiff(rownames(Ainv), ids_g)
  L11 <- Matrix::Cholesky(forceSymmetric(Ainv[oid, oid]), LDL = FALSE)
  A12 <- as.matrix(Ainv[oid, ids_g])
  A22inv <- as.matrix(Ainv[ids_g, ids_g]) - crossprod(A12, as.matrix(solve(L11, A12)))
  rm(L11, A12); A22 <- solve(A22inv)
  b <- (mean(diag(A22)) - mean(A22)) / (mean(diag(G)) - mean(G)); a <- mean(A22) - b * mean(G)
  Gb <- 0.95 * (a + b * G) + 0.05 * A22; rm(G, A22)
  Gbi <- solve(Gb)
  idx <- match(ids_g, rownames(Ainv)); ng <- length(idx)
  Hinv <- Ainv + sparseMatrix(i = rep(idx, times = ng), j = rep(idx, each = ng), x = as.vector(Gbi - A22inv),
                              dims = dim(Ainv))
  rm(A22inv); invisible(gc())
  # mixed-model equations: y = Xb + Za + e (records: genotyped + non-genotyped training cows)
  dd <- rbind(trn_g[, c("id", "breed", "bg", "hg", traits), with = FALSE],
              trn_ng[, c("id", "breed", "bg", "hg", traits), with = FALSE])
  X <- sparse.model.matrix(~ factor(bg) + factor(hg), data = dd)
  q <- qr(as.matrix(X)); X <- X[, q$pivot[seq_len(q$rank)], drop = FALSE]
  Za <- sparseMatrix(i = seq_len(nrow(dd)), j = match(as.character(dd$id), rownames(Ainv)),
                     x = 1, dims = c(nrow(dd), nrow(Ainv)))
  WW <- cbind(X, Za); nx <- ncol(X)
  CtC <- crossprod(WW)
  Hpad <- bdiag(Matrix(0, nx, nx, sparse = TRUE), Hinv)
  hh <- h2_mix(dd$breed)
  Y <- as.matrix(dd[, ..traits]); rhs <- as.matrix(crossprod(WW, Y))
  Lf <- NULL; u <- matrix(0, ncol(Mtr), nT)
  for (j in seq_len(nT)) {
    lam <- (1 - hh[j]) / hh[j]
    C <- forceSymmetric(CtC + lam * Hpad)
    Lf <- if (is.null(Lf)) Matrix::Cholesky(C, LDL = FALSE, super = TRUE) else update(Lf, C)
    sol <- as.vector(solve(Lf, rhs[, j], system = "A"))
    ahat <- sol[nx + idx]                                   # GEBV of genotyped training cows
    u[, j] <- as.vector(crossprod(Z, Gbi %*% ahat)) / k2pq  # back-solved SNP effects
  }
  colnames(u) <- traits; u
}
```

## Mate allocation with an inbreeding limit

Expected progeny inbreeding = genomic coancestry of sire and dam = G~sd~ / 2, with G built
from **base allele frequencies fixed at the end of burn-in**, so F is measured relative to
that base. Greedy allocation: each dam (random order) gets the highest-index sire whose
expected progeny F is below `r params$f_max` and who has not reached 2x his equal share of
matings. If no sire qualifies, the sire with the lowest coancestry is used.

```{r mate_fn}
coancestry <- function(Ms, dpop, p0) {          # dpop: dam population, genotypes pulled in chunks
  k <- 2 * sum(p0 * (1 - p0)); Zs <- sweep(Ms, 2, 2 * p0)
  do.call(cbind, lapply(split(seq_len(nInd(dpop)), ceiling(seq_len(nInd(dpop)) / 2000)), function(ix)
    tcrossprod(Zs, sweep(pullSnpGeno(dpop[ix], simParam = SP), 2, 2 * p0)) / k / 2))
}
allocate <- function(sire_idx, coan, n_mat, f_max, caps = NULL) {
  ns <- length(sire_idx); used <- integer(ns)
  cap <- if (is.null(caps)) rep(ceiling(2 * n_mat / ns), ns) else caps   # OCS passes its own caps
  stopifnot(sum(cap) >= n_mat)
  ord <- order(-sire_idx)
  dams <- sample(rep_len(seq_len(ncol(coan)), n_mat))
  plan <- matrix(NA_integer_, n_mat, 2)
  for (k in seq_along(dams)) {
    d <- dams[k]; ok <- ord[coan[ord, d] < f_max & used[ord] < cap[ord]]
    s <- if (length(ok)) ok[1] else { av <- which(used < cap); av[which.min(coan[av, d])] }
    used[s] <- used[s] + 1; plan[k, ] <- c(d, s)
  }
  list(plan = plan, expF = coan[cbind(plan[, 2], plan[, 1])])
}
```

## Optimum contribution selection (scenario GS_NTM_NUE35_OCS)

Following Meuwissen (1997, *J Anim Sci* 75:934), sire contributions **c** (summing to 1/2)
maximise the expected merit of the next generation, **c**'**g**, subject to the group
coancestry of all parents staying on a target path:

C(**c**) = **c**'K~mm~**c** + 2 **c**'K~mf~**c**~f~ + **c**~f~'K~ff~**c**~f~ ≤ C\*~t~,
with K = G/2 (genomic, base = end of burn-in) and fixed dam contributions **c**~f~.

The target follows the definition of the rate of inbreeding,
ΔF = (F~t+1~ - F~t~)/(1 - F~t~) (Falconer & Mackay), applied to coancestry:
C\*~t~ = C\*~t-1~ + ΔF (1 - C\*~t-1~), with ΔF = `r params$ocs_dF` per generation.
For comparison, the FAO guidelines for animal genetic resources target an effective size of
at least 50, equivalent to ΔF = 1% per generation. The correction term of Wellmann & Pfeiffer
(2009) for finite offspring numbers (of order 1/(4N)) is ignored, because N is ~10,000
offspring per breed per generation.

The problem is solved as a quadratic programme (`quadprog::solve.QP`): minimise
**c**'K~mm~**c** + 2**c**'K~mf~**c**~f~ - θ**c**'**g** subject to Σ**c** = 1/2, **c** ≥ 0. θ is
found by bisection as the largest value meeting the coancestry target. If even θ = 0
(minimum coancestry) exceeds the target, that generation is logged as infeasible and the
minimum-coancestry solution is used.

```{r ocs_fn}
# Zm: centred genotypes of candidate sires; zf: Z_d' c_f (female contribution summed over SNPs)
ocs_solve <- function(g, Zm, zf, k, C_target) {
  n <- length(g)
  Kmm <- tcrossprod(Zm) / (2 * k) + diag(1e-6, n)
  bm  <- as.vector(Zm %*% zf) / (2 * k)
  Cff <- sum(zf^2) / (2 * k)
  Amat <- cbind(rep(1, n), diag(n)); bv <- c(0.5, rep(0, n))
  sol_theta <- function(th) {
    x <- quadprog::solve.QP(Dmat = 2 * Kmm, dvec = th * g - 2 * bm, Amat = Amat,
                            bvec = bv, meq = 1)$solution
    x <- pmax(x, 0); x * 0.5 / sum(x)
  }
  Cof <- function(x) as.numeric(crossprod(x, Kmm %*% x)) + 2 * sum(x * bm) + Cff
  x0 <- sol_theta(0)
  if (Cof(x0) > C_target) return(list(c = x0, C = Cof(x0), feasible = FALSE, theta = 0))
  lo <- 0; hi <- 1e-3
  while (Cof(sol_theta(hi)) <= C_target && hi < 1e8) { lo <- hi; hi <- hi * 4 }
  for (it in 1:40) { mid <- (lo + hi) / 2; if (Cof(sol_theta(mid)) <= C_target) lo <- mid else hi <- mid }
  x <- sol_theta(lo)
  list(c = x, C = Cof(x), feasible = TRUE, theta = lo)
}
# integer matings per sire from contributions (largest-remainder rounding, total = n_mat)
contrib_to_caps <- function(cc, n_mat) {
  raw <- cc / sum(cc) * n_mat; cap <- floor(raw)
  rem <- n_mat - sum(cap); if (rem > 0) cap[order(-(raw - cap))[seq_len(rem)]] <- cap[order(-(raw - cap))[seq_len(rem)]] + 1
  cap
}
# centred genotype cross-products, chunk-wise
zt_c <- function(pop, cvec) Reduce(`+`, lapply(chunk_idx(nInd(pop)), function(ix)
  as.vector(crossprod(sweep(pullSnpGeno(pop[ix], simParam = SP), 2, 2 * p0), cvec[ix]))))
```

# Run the programmes

```{r run}
# Memory-lean helpers: process genotypes in row chunks of 2,000 animals
chunk_idx <- function(n, size = 2000) split(seq_len(n), ceiling(seq_len(n) / size))
geno_colsums <- function(pop) Reduce(`+`, lapply(chunk_idx(nInd(pop)), function(ix)
  colSums(pullSnpGeno(pop[ix], simParam = SP))))
# base allele frequencies = end of burn-in, all animals of all breeds
p0 <- Reduce(`+`, lapply(st$pop, geno_colsums)) / (2 * sum(sapply(st$pop, nInd)))
invisible(gc()); memlog("p0 done")
# genomic F relative to p0: diag(G) - 1, computed chunk-wise
genomic_F <- function(pop) unlist(lapply(chunk_idx(nInd(pop)), function(ix) {
  Z <- sweep(pullSnpGeno(pop[ix], simParam = SP), 2, 2 * p0)
  rowSums(Z^2) / (2 * sum(p0 * (1 - p0))) - 1 }))
# genomic EBV = (dosage - 1) %*% beta, chunk-wise
gebv <- function(pop, beta) do.call(rbind, lapply(chunk_idx(nInd(pop)), function(ix)
  (pullSnpGeno(pop[ix], simParam = SP) - 1) %*% beta))
scen <- intersect(scen_req, names(W_idx))
log_trend <- list(); log_beq <- list(); log_idx <- list(); log_F <- list(); log_ocs <- list(); log_time <- list()
ped0 <- fread(file.path(params$sim_dir, "pedigree.csv"))[, .(id = as.character(id), sire = as.character(sire), dam = as.character(dam))]

for (sc in scen) {
  # label: OCS runs with a non-default rate of inbreeding get their own name
  lab <- if (is_ocs(sc) && params$ocs_dF != 0.005) sprintf("%s_dF%g", sc, 100 * params$ocs_dF) else sc
  set.seed(params$seed + params$rep_id)     # same random stream start for every scenario within a replicate
  cur <- st$pop; hist_cows <- list(); prev_idx <- list(); C_star <- list()
  # Memory, 7 GB machine: the genomes of past cows are kept on disk (uncompressed, in the
  # R session's temporary folder) and read back only for the training set; phenotypes and herd blocks
  # stay in memory. The same cows are read back, so results are unchanged.
  hist_dir <- tempfile("hist_"); dir.create(hist_dir)
  if (length(scen) == 1) st$pop <- NULL   # Memory: one scenario per run, the start population is not needed again
  # Memory: PHENO has no genomic evaluation, so the burn-in cows (training set of the GS
  # scenarios) are never used; they were freed only inside the GS branch and PHENO was killed (out of memory).
  if (length(scen) == 1 && sc == "PHENO") { st$kept_cows <- NULL; invisible(gc()) }
  ped_all <- copy(ped0); ped_new <- list()
  for (g in seq_len(params$n_gs_gen)) {
    gen <- burn_end + g
    herd_z <- draw_herd_z(); nxt <- list()
    if (sc != "PHENO") {   # one multi-breed SNP-BLUP per generation, forward training only
    # training: cows of the previous two generations (forward only), stratified sample
    tr_keys <- names(hist_cows)[as.integer(sub(" .*", "", names(hist_cows))) %in% (g - 2):(g - 1)]
    if (!length(tr_keys)) {                          # first GS generation: burn-in cows
      trn <- phen0[generation %in% (burn_end - 1):burn_end]
      # Memory, 7 GB machine: the id order of the merged population is taken from the id
      # vectors, and each generation is subset to the sampled cows before merging. Same sample, same order.
      kp <- unname(st$kept_cows[paste(c(burn_end - 1, burn_end), rep(breeds, each = 2))])
      ids <- intersect(as.character(trn$id), unlist(lapply(kp, function(p) p@id)))
      ids <- sample(ids, min(length(ids), params$n_train_total))
      trpop <- do.call(c, lapply(kp, function(p) p[p@id %in% ids])); rm(kp)
      Mtr <- pullSnpGeno(trpop[match(ids, trpop@id)], simParam = SP)   # subset first (memory)
      trn_ng <- trn[!(as.character(id) %in% ids)]          # phenotyped, not in the genotyped sample
      trn <- trn[match(as.integer(ids), id)]
      Ytr <- as.matrix(trn[, ..traits]); Xdf <- trn[, .(breed, bg = paste(breed, generation),
                                                        hg = paste(herd, generation))]
      trn_ng[, `:=`(bg = paste(breed, generation), hg = paste(herd, generation))]
    } else {
      parts <- lapply(tr_keys, function(k) {
        h <- hist_cows[[k]]; data.table(id = h$id, breed = sub(".* ", "", k),
                                        bg = k, hg = paste(h$blk$herd, sub(" .*", "", k)), h$P) })
      trn <- rbindlist(parts)
      take <- sample(nrow(trn), min(nrow(trn), params$n_train_total))
      trn_ng <- trn[-take]; trn <- trn[take]
      trpop <- do.call(c, lapply(tr_keys, function(k) { hp <- readRDS(hist_cows[[k]]$file); hp[hp@id %in% trn$id] }))   # subset before merging (memory); match() below fixes the order
      Mtr <- pullSnpGeno(trpop[match(trn$id, trpop@id)], simParam = SP)   # subset first (memory)
      Ytr <- as.matrix(trn[, ..traits]); Xdf <- trn[, .(breed, bg, hg)]
    }
    rm(trpop); if (length(scen) == 1) st$kept_cows <- NULL; invisible(gc())   # free genomes before the evaluation (memory)
    memlog(paste("gen", g, "training matrix ready"))
    t_ev <- Sys.time()
    if (eval_model == "ssGBLUP") {
      trn_ng <- trn_ng[sample(.N, min(.N, params$n_nongeno_ss))]
      beta_g <- ss_gblup(Mtr, cbind(trn[, .(id = as.character(id))], Xdf, as.data.table(Ytr)),
                         trn_ng[, c("id", "breed", "bg", "hg", traits), with = FALSE][, id := as.character(id)], ped_all)
    } else beta_g <- snp_blup(Mtr, Ytr, Xdf)
    log_time[[paste(lab, g)]] <- data.table(scenario = lab, generation = gen, eval_model = eval_model,
      n_geno = nrow(Mtr), n_nongeno = if (eval_model == "ssGBLUP") nrow(trn_ng) else 0L,
      eval_sec = as.numeric(difftime(Sys.time(), t_ev, units = "secs")))
    rm(Mtr, Ytr); invisible(gc()); memlog(paste("gen", g, "evaluation done"))
    }
    for (b in breeds) {
      pop <- cur[[b]]
      cows  <- pop[pop@sex == "F"]; cows <- cows[seq_len(min(n_cow[[b]], nInd(cows)))]
      bulls <- pop[pop@sex == "M"]
      blk <- assign_blocks(nInd(cows), gen, b); P <- make_pheno(cows, b, blk, herd_z)
      Gg_c <- goal_G(cows); Gg_b <- goal_G(bulls)
      wv <- W_idx[[sc]][[b]]                                      # breed-specific weights
      Hc <- as.vector(sweep(Gg_c, 2, sdA0, `/`) %*% wv)   # true index value
      Hb <- as.vector(sweep(Gg_b, 2, sdA0, `/`) %*% wv)
      hfile <- file.path(hist_dir, paste0(g, "_", b, ".rds")); saveRDS(cows, hfile, compress = FALSE)
      hist_cows[[paste(g, b)]] <- list(file = hfile, id = cows@id, P = P, blk = blk)

      # ---- selection criterion ----
      if (sc == "PHENO") {
        Pc <- as.data.table(P)[, herd := blk$herd]
        Pc <- Pc[, (traits) := lapply(.SD, function(x) x - mean(x)), by = herd, .SDcols = traits]
        # phenotypic NTM index: herd-corrected phenotypes on the genetic-SD scale x NTM weights
        crit_c <- as.vector(sweep(as.matrix(Pc[, ..traits]), 2, sdA0, `/`) %*% wv); names(crit_c) <- cows@id
        crit_b <- if (is.null(prev_idx[[b]])) runif(nInd(bulls)) else prev_idx[[b]][bulls@mother]
        crit_b[is.na(crit_b)] <- 0; prev_idx[[b]] <- crit_c
      } else {
        ebv_c <- gebv(cows, beta_g)
        ebv_b <- gebv(bulls, beta_g)
        crit_c <- as.vector(sweep(ebv_c, 2, sdA0, `/`) %*% wv)
        crit_b <- as.vector(sweep(ebv_b, 2, sdA0, `/`) %*% wv)
        # index correlations: each trait's EBV with the estimated index
        log_idx[[paste(lab, g, b)]] <- data.table(scenario = lab, generation = gen, breed = b,
          trait = traits, cor_EBV_index = as.vector(cor(ebv_c, crit_c)),
          cor_TBV_goal = as.vector(cor(Gg_c, Hc)), acc_trait = diag(cor(ebv_c, Gg_c)))
      }

      # ---- truncation selection ----
      n_dam <- round(params$dam_prop * nInd(cows)); n_elite <- round(params$elite_dam_prop * nInd(cows))
      o_c <- order(-crit_c); dams <- cows[o_c[seq_len(n_dam)]]; elite <- cows[o_c[seq_len(n_elite)]]
      sires <- bulls[order(-crit_b)[seq_len(sires_n[[b]])]]
      sel_b <- order(-crit_b)[seq_len(sires_n[[b]])]
      w_b <- rep(1 / length(sel_b), length(sel_b))        # sire weights (equal use)
      if (is_ocs(sc)) {
        kk <- 2 * sum(p0 * (1 - p0))
        if (is.null(C_star[[b]])) {                      # C*_0 = current mean coancestry
          zall <- zt_c(cows, rep(0.5 / nInd(cows), nInd(cows))) + zt_c(bulls, rep(0.5 / nInd(bulls), nInd(bulls)))
          C_star[[b]] <- sum(zall^2) / (2 * kk)
        }
        C_star[[b]] <- C_star[[b]] + params$ocs_dF * (1 - C_star[[b]])
        cand <- order(-crit_b)[seq_len(min(params$ocs_n_cand, nInd(bulls)))]
        cf <- 0.25 / n_dam + 0.25 * (seq_len(n_dam) <= n_elite) / n_elite   # dams sorted: elite first
        zf <- zt_c(dams, cf)
        Zm <- sweep(pullSnpGeno(bulls[cand], simParam = SP), 2, 2 * p0)
        oc <- ocs_solve(crit_b[cand], Zm, zf, kk, C_star[[b]])
        keep <- oc$c > 1e-5
        sel_b <- cand[keep]; w_b <- oc$c[keep] / sum(oc$c[keep])
        sires <- bulls[sel_b]
        log_ocs[[paste(lab, g, b)]] <- data.table(scenario = lab, generation = gen, breed = b,
          C_target = C_star[[b]], C_achieved = oc$C, feasible = oc$feasible,
          n_sires_used = sum(keep), max_share = max(w_b), theta = oc$theta)
        rm(Zm); invisible(gc())
      }

      # ---- breeder's equation (index scale) ----
      r_m <- cor(crit_b, Hb); r_f <- cor(crit_c, Hc)
      i_m <- (sum(w_b * crit_b[sel_b]) - mean(crit_b)) / sd(crit_b)   # contribution-weighted
      i_f <- (mean(crit_c[o_c[seq_len(n_dam)]]) - mean(crit_c)) / sd(crit_c)     # dams of daughters
      i_fe <- (mean(crit_c[o_c[seq_len(n_elite)]]) - mean(crit_c)) / sd(crit_c)  # dams of sons (elite)
      log_beq[[paste(lab, g, b)]] <- data.table(scenario = lab, generation = gen, breed = b,
        p_male = length(sel_b) / nInd(bulls), p_female = n_dam / nInd(cows),
        i_male_theory = trunc_i(length(sel_b) / nInd(bulls)), i_male_obs = i_m,
        i_female_theory = trunc_i(n_dam / nInd(cows)), i_female_obs = i_f,
        S_male = sum(w_b * crit_b[sel_b]) - mean(crit_b), S_female = mean(crit_c[o_c[seq_len(n_dam)]]) - mean(crit_c),
        r_male = r_m, r_female = r_f, sdH_male = sd(Hb), sdH_female = sd(Hc),
        i_elite_theory = trunc_i(n_elite / nInd(cows)), i_elite_obs = i_fe,
        # four-path equation (Rendel & Robertson 1950), discrete generations (L = 1):
        # sires of sons = sires of daughters; dams of sons = elite tier; dams of daughters = dam tier
        dG_expected = (2 * i_m * r_m * sd(Hb) + (i_fe + i_f) * r_f * sd(Hc)) / 4,
        meanH = mean(c(Hb, Hc)))

      # ---- trends (all traits) ----
      Gown <- own_country_G(cows, blk$country); colnames(Gown) <- traits
      log_trend[[paste(lab, g, b)]] <- data.table(scenario = lab, generation = gen, breed = b,
        trait = traits, mean_G = colMeans(Gown), var_G = apply(Gown, 2, var),
        mean_P = colMeans(P), var_P = apply(P, 2, var))

      # ---- mating ----
      nf <- n_cow[[b]]
      if (is_mate(sc)) {
        Ms <- pullSnpGeno(sires, simParam = SP)
        coanF <- coancestry(Ms, dams, p0)
        coanM <- coancestry(Ms, elite, p0)
        caps <- if (is_ocs(sc)) contrib_to_caps(w_b, 2 * nf) else NULL
        aF <- allocate(crit_b[sel_b], coanF, 2 * nf, params$f_max, caps)
        aM <- allocate(crit_b[sel_b], coanM, 2 * nf, params$f_max, caps)
        fem  <- makeCross2(dams,  sires, aF$plan, nProgeny = 1)
        male <- makeCross2(elite, sires, aM$plan, nProgeny = 1)
        expF <- mean(c(aF$expF, aM$expF))
      } else {
        fem  <- randCross2(dams,  sires, nCrosses = 2 * nf, nProgeny = 1)
        male <- randCross2(elite, sires, nCrosses = 2 * nf, nProgeny = 1)
        Ms <- pullSnpGeno(sires, simParam = SP)
        expF <- mean(coancestry(Ms, dams, p0))
      }
      # AlphaSimR sexes are systematic (half F, half M): 2*nf crosses per path,
      # daughters kept from the dam path, sons from the elite-dam path
      nxt[[b]] <- c(fem[fem@sex == "F"], male[male@sex == "M"]); rm(fem, male)
      memlog(paste("gen", g, b, "offspring made"))
      ped_new[[b]] <- data.table(id = nxt[[b]]@id, sire = nxt[[b]]@father, dam = nxt[[b]]@mother)
      # genomic inbreeding of the new generation relative to the burn-in base
      F_g <- genomic_F(nxt[[b]])
      log_F[[paste(lab, g, b)]] <- data.table(scenario = lab, generation = gen + 1, breed = b,
                                             F_genomic = mean(F_g), expected_F = expF)
      # Memory: this breed's parent generation is no longer needed (its cows stay in hist_cows)
      cur[b] <- list(NULL); rm(pop, cows, bulls, dams, elite, sires); invisible(gc())
    }
    cur <- nxt
    ped_all <- rbind(ped_all, rbindlist(ped_new)); ped_new <- list()
    # keep only the last two generations of cows (all that training uses)
    old <- as.integer(sub(" .*", "", names(hist_cows))) < g - 1
    for (k in names(hist_cows)[old]) unlink(hist_cows[[k]]$file)
    hist_cows[old] <- NULL; invisible(gc())
    progress(sc, " gen ", gen, " done ", format(Sys.time() - t0))
  }
}
trend <- rbindlist(log_trend); beq <- rbindlist(log_beq)
idx <- rbindlist(log_idx); Fdt <- rbindlist(log_F); ocs <- rbindlist(log_ocs); ev_time <- rbindlist(log_time)
```

# Response to selection: breeder's equation

Expected change per generation on the true index scale, four-path equation
(Rendel & Robertson 1950) with discrete generations (L = 1 on every path):
ΔG~exp~ = [2 i~m~ r~m~ σ~H,m~ + (i~DS~ + i~DD~) r~f~ σ~H,f~] / 4, where the same sires breed sons
and daughters, i~DS~ is the intensity on the elite dams of sons (top `r params$elite_dam_prop*100`%)
and i~DD~ on the dams of daughters (top `r params$dam_prop*100`%).
Observed ΔG = change in the mean true index of candidates from one generation to the next.

```{r beq}
beq[, dG_observed := shift(meanH, type = "lead") - meanH, by = .(scenario, breed)]
kable(beq[, .(i_m_theory = mean(i_male_theory), i_m_obs = mean(i_male_obs),
              i_DS_obs = mean(i_elite_obs), i_DD_obs = mean(i_female_obs),
              r_m = mean(r_male), r_f = mean(r_female),
              dG_exp = mean(dG_expected), dG_obs = mean(dG_observed, na.rm = TRUE)),
          by = .(scenario, breed)], digits = 3,
      caption = "Averages over generations (index in standardised genetic units)")
ggplot(beq[!is.na(dG_observed)], aes(dG_expected, dG_observed, colour = scenario)) +
  geom_abline(lty = 2) + geom_point() + facet_wrap(~breed) + theme_bw() +
  labs(title = "Observed vs expected response per generation")
```

**Expectation:** observed < expected over time, because the breeder's equation ignores the
loss of genetic variance from selection (Bulmer effect), drift and inbreeding.

```{r trends, fig.width=11, fig.height=8}
  rbindlist(lapply(scen, function(s) cbind(scenario = s, trend0))),
  trend, fill = TRUE)
long <- melt(tr_all[trait %in% c("MY", "NUE", "MUN", "SF", "CH4", "ICF")],
             id.vars = c("scenario", "generation", "breed", "trait"))
ggplot(long[breed == "HOL"], aes(generation, value, colour = scenario)) +
  geom_line() + geom_vline(xintercept = burn_end + 0.5, lty = 3) +
  facet_grid(variable ~ trait, scales = "free_y") + theme_bw() +
  labs(title = "Holstein: mean and variance of genetic (G) and phenotypic (P) values",
       subtitle = "dotted line = start of genomic selection", y = "standardised units")
```

```{r nue_trend}
kable(dcast(trend[trait %in% c("NUE", "MUN", "MY", "SF", "CH4") & generation == max(generation)],
            breed + trait ~ scenario, value.var = "mean_G"), digits = 3,
      caption = "Mean genetic value in the final generation (genetic SD units of the founders)")
```

# Multi-trait information over cycles: correlation with the index

```{r idx_cor, fig.width=10, fig.height=4}
if (nrow(idx) == 0) cat("No genomic EBVs in this run (PHENO scenario only) - nothing to show.\n") else print(
ggplot(idx[breed == "HOL"], aes(generation, cor_EBV_index, colour = trait)) +
  geom_line() + facet_wrap(~scenario) + theme_bw() +
  labs(y = "cor(EBV of trait, index)", title = "How strongly each trait drives the index (Holstein)"))
if (nrow(idx)) kable(dcast(idx[, .(acc = mean(acc_trait)), by = .(scenario, trait)], trait ~ scenario,
            value.var = "acc"), digits = 3, caption = "Mean accuracy of genomic EBV per trait")
```

# Inbreeding and the mating plan

```{r inbreeding}
ggplot(Fdt, aes(generation, F_genomic, colour = scenario)) + geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = params$f_max, lty = 2) + facet_wrap(~breed) + theme_bw() +
  labs(y = "mean genomic F (relative to end of burn-in)")
kable(Fdt[generation == max(generation)], digits = 4)
```

**Reading the inbreeding results.** The F < `r params$f_max` limit in GS_NTM_NUE35_MATE applies to
the *expected inbreeding of each mating*. It does not limit the *rate* of inbreeding of the
population, which is set mainly by how many sires are used and how related they are. With
about one sire per 200 cows and truncation selection on GEBV, selected bulls cluster in few
families. If mean F rises well above `r params$f_max` in every scenario, mate allocation alone
cannot meet the target. The established remedy is **optimum contribution selection**
(Meuwissen 1997, *J Anim Sci* 75:934), which chooses sires *and* their number of matings to
maximise genetic gain subject to a fixed rate of coancestry increase. It is the next step to
implement in this pipeline, not something the current results show to be satisfied.

## Optimum contribution selection diagnostics

```{r ocs_diag}
if (nrow(ocs)) {
  kable(ocs, digits = 4, caption = "OCS per generation: coancestry target vs achieved, feasibility, sires used, largest sire share")
  print(ggplot(ocs, aes(generation)) + geom_line(aes(y = C_target), lty = 2) +
          geom_line(aes(y = C_achieved, colour = breed)) + theme_bw() +
          labs(y = "group coancestry of parents", subtitle = "dashed = target path"))
} else cat("OCS scenario not run in this render.\n")
```

# Recommended mating plan (final generation)

The allocation actually used in the last generation of `GS_NTM_NUE35_MATE` is reported per breed:
number of sires used, matings per sire, and the expected progeny inbreeding.

```{r plan}
kable(Fdt[scenario == "GS_NTM_NUE35_MATE", .(mean_expected_F = mean(expected_F)), by = breed], digits = 4)
```

```{r save}
tag <- paste(scen, collapse = "_")
if (length(scen) == 1 && is_ocs(scen) && params$ocs_dF != 0.005) tag <- lab
if (params$eval_model != "auto") tag <- paste0(tag, "_", eval_model)   # model-test runs carry the model name
if (params$rep_id > 0) tag <- paste0(tag, "_rep", params$rep_id)
if (nrow(ev_time)) fwrite(ev_time, file.path(params$sim_dir, paste0("gs_eval_time_", tag, ".csv")))
fwrite(trend, file.path(params$sim_dir, paste0("gs_trend_", tag, ".csv")))
fwrite(beq,   file.path(params$sim_dir, paste0("gs_breeders_equation_", tag, ".csv")))
fwrite(idx,   file.path(params$sim_dir, paste0("gs_index_correlations_", tag, ".csv")))
fwrite(Fdt,   file.path(params$sim_dir, paste0("gs_inbreeding_", tag, ".csv")))
if (nrow(ocs)) fwrite(ocs, file.path(params$sim_dir, paste0("gs_ocs_", tag, ".csv")))
fwrite(data.table(trait = traits, sdA0 = sdA0), file.path(params$sim_dir, "gs_sdA0.csv"))   # standardisation constants (same in every run)
cat("Run time:", format(Sys.time() - t0), "\n")
```
